security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, JavaScript template literals, and inline code. The setup command executes an NPM package, while examples automatically execute learned recommendations and record complete command strings. Publication should require safeguards for package installation, operation approval, and command-log redaction.

remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited package version and require explicit approval before running npx. Document package integrity verification and installation effects.
Validate recommendations against an allowlist, separate commands from arguments, block destructive actions, and require human approval before execution.
Redact credentials, tokens, private paths, and secret-bearing arguments before storing operation history. Document retention and deletion controls.

content.user_title: Coordinate AI Agents with Agentic Jujutsu
content.value_statement: Concurrent AI agents can create conflicting changes and repeat failed workflows. This skill documents Agentic Jujutsu methods for coordination, trajectory learning, and integrity checks.
actual_capabilities: Initialize JjWrapper and perform status, commit, log, diff, branch, and rebase operations.
Record task trajectories with operations, outcome scores, and critiques for later learning.
Retrieve learned suggestions, discovered patterns, similar trajectories, and progress statistics.
Coordinate multiple wrapper instances for concurrent development, review, and testing workflows.
Generate and verify SHA3-512 fingerprints and configure documented trajectory encryption.
Inspect operation counts, success rates, durations, and recent command history.
limitations: Requires the external agentic-jujutsu NPM package and a compatible JavaScript runtime.
It does not implement wrapper methods or verify package behavior, benchmarks, or cryptographic guarantees.
Several examples depend on undefined deployment, review, and task-execution helpers.
Learned recommendations reflect recorded trajectories and may contain unsafe or outdated operations.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Concurrent Development
use_cases.description: Coordinate independent code changes across multiple AI agents while recording outcomes for later workflow suggestions.

use_cases.title: Improve Deployment Workflows
use_cases.description: Track deployment trajectories, compare prior outcomes, and review suggested operations before running them.

use_cases.title: Check Repository Integrity
use_cases.description: Generate integrity fingerprints and evaluate encryption workflows without assuming documented guarantees are independently verified.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Repository State
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agentic Jujutsu to inspect this repository and summarize status. Do not modify files or run installation commands without approval.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Task Trajectory
prompt_templates.prompt: Track my task as a trajectory, record relevant version-control operations, and ask for an honest outcome score before finalizing.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan independent branches for three agents, identify overlap, and propose a concurrent commit sequence using Agentic Jujutsu.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Learned Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review ReasoningBank recommendations for this deployment. Validate every operation, flag destructive steps, and request approval before execution.

output_examples.input: Inspect this repository without making changes.
output_examples.output: The repository status is summarized. No commit, branch, rebase, installation, or network action is performed.

output_examples.input: Summarize learning after ten completed trajectories.
output_examples.output: The summary covers trajectory count, patterns, average success, improvement rate, prediction accuracy, and low-confidence areas.

output_examples.input: Plan concurrent work for three agents.
output_examples.output: Three independent work areas are proposed, with overlap checks, branch ownership, and a review checkpoint before commits.

best_practices: Use specific task descriptions and record honest outcome scores with concise critiques.
Review learned suggestions against repository state and require approval before destructive or networked operations.
Redact secrets from commands and trajectory context before storing operation history.
anti_patterns: Do not execute unpinned external packages without verifying provenance and obtaining approval.
Do not run learned operations automatically or treat confidence scores as authorization.
Do not inflate success scores or omit failures, because distorted trajectories weaken later suggestions.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides documented workflows and examples for Agentic Jujutsu version control, trajectory learning, operation tracking, coordination, and integrity checks.

faq.question: Does the skill include Agentic Jujutsu?
faq.answer: No. It references the external agentic-jujutsu NPM package and contains guidance rather than an embedded implementation.

faq.question: Can it run without JavaScript?
faq.answer: The examples use JavaScript and asynchronous APIs. Other integrations require compatible bindings that this skill does not document.

faq.question: Are learned suggestions safe to execute automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review each operation, validate arguments, block destructive actions, and obtain approval before execution.

faq.question: What does quantum-resistant mean here?
faq.answer: The guide documents SHA3-512 fingerprints and HQC-128 trajectory encryption. It does not independently verify implementation or security guarantees.

faq.question: Does it replace Git?
faq.answer: The guide presents Agentic Jujutsu workflows and some Git comparisons. Confirm repository compatibility and migration requirements before changing version-control tools.
